parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure JavaScript ESM .mjs output in /output, local imports with suffixes, manual argv parsing for --a and --b, base58 encode/decode behavior, Python bytes repr formatting, no npm dependencies, and black-box executable observation.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed executable behavior, then delegated codecs to agent-0 and argument parsing to agent-1 while reserving the entry file and integrated verification for itself.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 implemented manual UTF-8, base58 digit-array conversion, and bytes repr. Agent-1 implemented parseArgs. The parent wrote test7.mjs importing args.mjs, utf8.mjs, base58.mjs, and pyrepr.mjs, including special handling for ValueError-style invalid base58 input.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent received a completed AgentSwarm result, wrote the entry file into /output, read the generated library files, and delivered test7.mjs plus lib/args.mjs, lib/base58.mjs, lib/pyrepr.mjs, and lib/utf8.mjs as the artifact set.
parallel.verification: Children ran syntax and module-specific smoke tests. The parent ran sample comparisons and additional edge comparisons against the executable, observed diffs for process id and program-name cases, then treated them as acceptable and closed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official completed evaluator still failed the solution at 80/141. The mounted evidence does not expose testcase-level failures, so the remaining defects are known only at aggregate level.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same pure ESM, .mjs, local import, manual argument parsing, base58, bytes repr, no npm dependency, and executable-observation requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned all code, integration, testing, and final response with no delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: The actor wrote utf8.mjs, base58.mjs using BigInt arithmetic, pyrepr.mjs, argparse.mjs with a simpler parser, and test7.mjs wiring those modules together.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor wrote all deliverable files directly into /output and the artifact validation recorded test7.mjs plus lib/base58.mjs, lib/argparse.mjs, lib/pyrepr.mjs, and lib/utf8.mjs.
serial.verification: The actor ran sample comparisons and edge comparisons against the executable, including empty inputs, leading-zero decode, non-ASCII input, --arg=value syntax, and missing argument behavior.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official completed evaluator still failed the solution at 80/141. Testcase-level failures are not mounted, so the exact hidden failure set cannot be reconstructed from available inputs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, .mjs, local import, manual argv, base58, bytes repr, executable-observation, and no external dependency constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task requirements and wrote an equivalent file set with no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the official outcome; both saw the same task and both failed the same aggregate official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent split work into codec modules for agent-0 and args.mjs for agent-1, while parent owned entry-file assembly and integrated checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor owned all modules, the entry point, verification, and closure directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed into completed child-owned modules; serial used one local owner. The split did not leave an owner gap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent gave each child explicit output paths, export signatures, accepted behaviors, and the instruction that the entry file belonged elsewhere.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used local module names and imports inside one actor, with no inter-agent handoff boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit cross-agent interface contracts for parseArgs, b58encode, b58decode, utf8Encode, and bytesRepr; no incompatible child contract is visible.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented digit-array base58 conversion, a stricter args parser, Python bytes repr, and entry-level invalid-character handling.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented BigInt base58 conversion, a simpler argparse module, bytes repr, and an entry point without the same delegated module split.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations differ internally, but both produced artifacts that passed local sample checks and failed the same official aggregate score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both child agents completed and the AgentSwarm result returned to the parent before the parent wrote and tested the entry file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; all results were local writes in order.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not lose, trap, or ignore a completed child result; serial had no analogous result boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child agents wrote distinct library files under /output/lib and the parent later wrote test7.mjs importing the agreed names.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files directly with a different parser filename, argparse.mjs, and imported that filename from test7.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared output directory but with distinct file ownership and no observed overwrite or incompatible merge; serial avoided shared-state coordination by construction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children and parent ran syntax, module, sample, and edge tests; the parent saw some local diff output for dynamic process-id and program-name cases but treated it as acceptable before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample and edge tests and similarly treated its limited local checks as enough, while the official evaluator later failed the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local black-box samples and edge cases rather than evaluator-complete acceptance evidence; this is a shared verification limitation, not a distinct parallel coordination failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed within budget after 461.84 agent seconds and 547.426 cell seconds, using two subagents and no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed within budget after 137.52 agent seconds and 223.154 cell seconds, using no subagents and no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more time and tokens, but did not timeout or leave children pending. The longer budget use is not by itself a retained load or timing pattern.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed status records report solution_passed false and 80/141. Parallel and serial solved the visible samples through different workflows, but neither delivered a fully accepted migration. The available mounted evidence supports a contrast in coordination style and implementation choices, not a parallel-specific cause for an outcome gap.
parallel_contributors: Parallel completed child-owned codec and parser modules and parent-owned entry assembly before local checks.
Parallel accepted local sample and edge-check evidence despite later official failure.
serial_contributors: Serial implemented all modules and entry code in one actor and accepted local sample and edge-check evidence despite later official failure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a manual digit-array base58 implementation and args.mjs; serial used BigInt base58 and argparse.mjs.
Parallel added ValueError-style invalid base58 handling in the entry point; serial threw a simpler JavaScript Error path for invalid characters.
evaluator_effects: The pair inputs expose only aggregate official pass counts, not testcase-level failure reasons.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; comparative process contrast only

The parent explicitly integrated child modules by writing test7.mjs after the swarm returned; no unowned reconciliation step is visible.
The parent retained assembly ownership for the entry file and final artifact placement.
The parent controlled the end-to-end transition from executable probing to delegation, assembly, verification, and closure.
The parent performed quick executable observations before delegation, but productive implementation then ran in child agents and no delay consequence displaced required work.
Executable probing was brief and followed by completed implementation and integrated checks; there was no separate investigation phase that left implementation deadline-constrained or incomplete.
The indispensable path, entry assembly and integrated verification, was owned by the parent and completed before closure; no auxiliary work starved it.
The fan-out was only two children, both completed, and the run did not timeout; higher token use alone is not budget exhaustion.
The codec child received multiple modules but completed and returned usable work; no child scope is shown unfinished or unable to checkpoint.
The child briefs included the relevant task, environment, output paths, export signatures, no external dependency rule, and verification expectations for their scopes.
The parent specified exact module paths and exported signatures, and the parent entry file imported those names after the child results returned.
No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing between parent and children; the returned swarm result preserved the relevant completion summaries.
The AgentSwarm result was long but the parent proceeded to assembly, file reads, and tests; there is no visible inability to consume a needed handoff.
No child result described superseded workspace or requirement state that the parent then consumed incorrectly.
The two child results covered different modules and did not provide incompatible reports or contracts requiring adjudication.

Although the official hidden evaluation failed, the parent did run integrated executable comparisons after assembly; the visible verification gap is shared with serial and is not a parallel-specific completion based only on workflow return or component checks.
There was no retry or replacement child in the parallel trajectory.

No verifier child was used; module test findings and parent integrated checks were visible in the parent or child timelines.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; both returned completed work.

The parent waited for a normal AgentSwarm completion, not a timeout or near-deadline wait without inspecting available progress.
The children wrote different files with non-overlapping scopes: codecs versus argument parsing. No competing design required reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file.

Agents wrote in a shared /output tree, but ownership was separated by file and no unstable state, provenance loss, collision, or overwrite consequence is visible.
No generated fixture, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary artifact from one actor was consumed by another as a reference environment.
